exa1: Tokio is an asynchronous runtime for the Rust programming language. It provides the building blocks needed for writing network applications. It gives the flexibility to target a wide range of systems, from large servers with dozens of cores to small embedded devices. Tokio's APIs are memory-safe, thread-safe, and misuse-resistant. This helps prevent common bugs, such as unbounded queues, buffer overflows, and task starvation. Building on top of Rust, Tokio provides a multi-threaded, work-stealing scheduler.
